entries.03c8e3b72d03565c: This business makes relays, switches and connectors that connect and disconnect electrical current, as well as sensors that serve as the eyes and ears of machines. The annual securities report states that its mission is “to create value for customers and contribute to people and society on Earth with our devices and modules,” and that it provides these worldwide to customers in a wide range of industries, including EV and mobility, energy infrastructure, consumer electronics and industrial equipment. However, this business has been classified as [[term:discontinued-operations|discontinued operations]] from the fiscal year ended March 2026, following the board of directors' decision on March 30, 2026 to carry out a company split (absorption-type split) and to transfer shares of the successor company. As a result, it is excluded from the [[term:segment|segment]] revenue table, and the revenue and operating profit of this business alone are not printed in the segment information of the annual securities report. What can be determined is the number of employees, 6,122 (as of March 31, 2026), and current assets of ¥127.2 billion and current liabilities of ¥40.6 billion included in the consolidated balance sheet. The company has resolved to transfer shares of the successor company in October 2026, and this business is scheduled to leave the Group.

entries.100c2c487dd4da5f: It manufactures and sells devices and services for four entirely different settings (factories, homes and hospitals, stations and roads, and health insurance associations) and earns revenue from them. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] describes the scope of its products as “extending across the entire field of industrial control equipment components and system equipment, and further to life and public-related equipment and systems.” The ways of selling are not uniform. Control devices and healthcare are mass-production businesses in which revenue is recognized when the product arrives at the customer; the annual securities report explains: “The group’s production and sales items are wide-ranging and diverse; even products of the same type do not necessarily have uniform capacity, structure or format, and many products are not made to order, so the group does not present production scale or order scale by amount for each [[term:segment|segment]].” This means that it does not receive consolidated orders from specific large customers. In contrast, the social systems business recognizes revenue “once customer acceptance has generally been obtained”; it involves installation and on-site adjustment work, and for long-term construction contracts it recognizes revenue according to the degree of progress. The data solutions business receives payment through its [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiary]] JMDC Inc. for having pharmaceutical companies and insurance companies use anonymized data derived from health insurance associations and medical institutions. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥767,351 million; revenue from external customers by breakdown was: control devices ¥409,478 million, healthcare ¥145,258 million, social systems ¥144,257 million, data solutions ¥51,151 million, and eliminations, adjustments and others ¥17,207 million.
entries.15343c190594c09b: Users of medical devices in over 130 countries (home users and medical settings)
entries.1f7e964b47efa7d6: At the root is a single concept: the “core technology of ‘Sensing & Control + Think’.” Combining sensors that measure the position or state of objects, controllers that determine the next movement from measured values, and relays that connect or cut electricity, it sells them as control devices in factories, as blood pressure monitors and thermometers in homes and hospitals, and as automatic ticket gates and traffic control systems in stations and on roads. The same technology is sold in different markets in different forms. In recent years, a service using data collected from devices has been added to this.

entries.48ff94391249ce4a: This business makes and sells health and medical devices usable both at home and in medical settings. The annual securities report states that, with the mission of “contributing to healthy and vibrant lives for each person on Earth,” it provides “medical devices and services that are easy to use, allowing anyone to measure simply and accurately, and that are committed to the accuracy and quality needed for use in medical settings.” It sells blood pressure monitors, thermometers and nebulizers (devices for inhaling asthma medication), among other products, in more than 130 countries, in line with each country's medical device certification. The smartphone health management app “OMRON connect” has been downloaded more than 15 million times cumulatively in over 130 countries and regions, and the company is also expanding its remote patient monitoring service, under which physicians view patients' daily vital data from remote locations, mainly in Europe and the United States. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥145,258 million, operating profit was ¥15.4 billion, the operating margin was 10.6%, and the number of employees was 4,004. By region, revenue was Greater China ¥37,310 million, Europe ¥34,783 million, the Americas ¥29,507 million, Japan ¥24,110 million, and Southeast Asia and Others ¥19,092 million, making it a business in which overseas revenue exceeds domestic revenue. The company explains that, although regions excluding China were firm, the sharp decline in China in the first quarter meant full-year revenue stayed at the prior-year level, and that operating profit fell significantly due to intensifying competition in the main price range of blood pressure monitors and the effects of U.S. tariff policy.

entries.8d1770c2d2e6e5de: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥767,351 million. Most of it comes from the sale of equipment, but the company is shifting its weight toward data services. The securities report puts the data service revenue ratio for fiscal 2025 at 9% and states that the company aims for revenue of more than ¥100 billion from the Data Service Business in fiscal 2027. Although the Data Solutions Business's revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026, ¥51,151 million, was the smallest of its 4 continuing businesses, the number of IDs issued for the health information platform 'Pep Up' grew, and transaction value with pharmaceutical companies and insurers that use anonymized processed data also increased.
entries.90b4e31a61b2e670: This is the newest business, selling services that use data gathered from equipment. The company states that it aims to evolve the entire Group from manufacturing into a solutions business (products + services), and that it established the Data Solutions Business Division in December 2023. At the center is JMDC Inc., a medical statistics data service that joined the Group in October 2023 and is a [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiary]] with 54.3% of voting rights; the number of IDs issued for the health information platform “Pep Up” increased, and transaction amounts with pharmaceutical companies and insurance companies using anonymized data derived from health insurance societies and medical institutions also rose. The aim of this business is to combine field data obtained from equipment in the Control Equipment, Healthcare and Social Systems businesses. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥51,151 million, operating profit was ¥3.6 billion, the operating margin was 7.1%, and the number of employees was 2,603. Almost all revenue is domestic, with revenue from Japan at ¥50,580 million. The company states that it aims for data service business revenue of over ¥100 billion in fiscal 2027; although it is the smallest of the four businesses, its target for average annual revenue growth of +23.0% toward fiscal 2030 is set as the highest among the four businesses.

entries.9a6300d46212c259: The group consists of OMRON Corporation, headquartered in Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto, 163 subsidiaries (75 in Japan and 88 overseas) and 10 associated companies (7 in Japan and 3 overseas) (as of March 31, 2026). Headcount is 26,050. The company has a distinctive way of organizing itself; the history section of the annual securities report states that in 1955 it devised the “producer system” (a method of separating out production subsidiaries). The approach of separating companies by product and by region still persists; core companies are set up for each business, such as OMRON Healthcare Co., Ltd. and OMRON Social Solutions Co., Ltd., and companies overseeing regions are lined up overseas as well. JMDC Inc., a medical statistics data services company, is a [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiary]] in which the company holds 54.3% of the voting rights.

entries.a7ecaf8d1b2ce76c: The securities report does not disclose information on major customers, and no single customer exceeding 1 tenth of sales is listed. Customers are also widely spread across regions: sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥348,638 million in Japan, ¥144,131 million in Greater China, ¥116,770 million in Europe, ¥82,039 million in Southeast Asia and others, and ¥73,283 million in the Americas. However, each business looks quite different: Industrial Automation and Healthcare are larger overseas, while Social Systems, with sales to external customers of ¥144,257 million, sells ¥142,793 million of that in Japan and is almost entirely a domestic business.
entries.ac567abb6dff26e0: This business makes and sells equipment for running, measuring and stopping factory machinery. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] describes this business as one that, under the vision of “Creating a rich future for people, industry and the planet through automation,” innovates manufacturing worldwide with advanced automation based on the core technology of “Sensing & Control + Think.” It offers a wide range of components, including sensors (parts that measure the position or condition of objects), controllers (devices that give instructions to machines), relays, safety devices and image processing systems, and it sets out the concept of “i-Automation!,” which combines these to solve factory challenges. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥409,478 million, the largest of the four continuing businesses and more than half of the company-wide revenue of ¥767,351 million. Operating profit was ¥42.8 billion, the operating margin was 10.4%, and the number of employees was 8,778. Customers are spread widely across regions; by region, revenue from external customers in the same fiscal year was Japan ¥123,787 million, Greater China ¥105,468 million, Europe ¥81,987 million, Southeast Asia and Others ¥54,621 million, and the Americas ¥43,615 million. The company explains that, although capital investment related to EVs stalled, demand related to generative AI was firm, and the launch of new products tailored to customer needs in each region as planned also contributed, so revenue rose significantly.
entries.afb7023a1b2064c3: This business provides equipment and services that support social infrastructure such as stations, roads and electricity. The annual securities report describes this business as one whose mission is “creating a rich society in which people around the world can continue to live securely, safely and comfortably.” It handles energy-related products such as energy storage systems and photovoltaic power conditioners, station operation systems represented by automatic ticket gates and ticket vending machines, traffic control and road management systems, UPS (uninterruptible power supply) and infrastructure monitoring, and it also provides M&S (Management & Services), which covers everything from engineering to operation management and maintenance. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥144,257 million and operating profit was ¥19.7 billion, and the operating margin of 13.7% is the highest of the four continuing businesses. The number of employees was 2,311. Almost all revenue is domestic; revenue from Japan in the same fiscal year was ¥142,793 million, accounting for the bulk of revenue from external customers. The company explains that revenue increased because energy storage systems remained firm amid growing demand for self-consumption of renewable energy and the use of subsidy programs, and station operation systems also saw stable capital investment demand against the backdrop of recovering passenger numbers; and that operating profit rose significantly through cost reductions in manufacturing costs and appropriate pricing.

entries.b8eb237ef38559cf: For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue was ¥767.4 billion, operating profit was ¥59.9 billion, and operating margin was 7.8% (the securities report prints these figures in these units in its table of financial targets). Profitability differs by business: segment operating profit was ¥42.8 billion for Control Devices, ¥19.7 billion for Social Systems, ¥15.4 billion for Healthcare and ¥3.6 billion for Data Solutions. Control Devices, the largest business by revenue, is also the largest by profit, but the highest operating margin is Social Systems at 13.7%, compared with 10.4% for Control Devices, 10.6% for Healthcare and 7.1% for Data Solutions. The company explains that gross profit margin fell due to rising raw material prices, higher logistics costs and the impact of U.S. tariff policy, but operating profit increased year on year thanks to revenue growth and control of fixed costs.
